# KBD Constraints — Prior Authorization Workbench

These constraints are derived from the repository documentation and its Rust,
React/Vite, Tauri, and Flutter architecture. KBD and every executing tool must
apply them before a change can be archived.

## Blocking Constraints

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: "All build-only surfaces must compile or analyze successfully"
    command: "cargo build --workspace && pnpm --dir web build && flutter analyze mobile"

  - id: invariant-tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    description: "Rust domain invariants and Flutter tests must pass"
    command: "cargo test --workspace && flutter test mobile"

  - id: architecture-audit-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: "The repository architecture audit must pass"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: three-evidence-states
    severity: blocking
    description: "Evidence state must preserve met, gap, and void as distinct values"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: clinical-authority-boundary
    severity: blocking
    description: "Administrative authority must never imply permission to affirm a clinical gate or sign a letter"
    command: "cargo test --workspace"

  - id: host-remains-shell-neutral
    severity: blocking
    description: "aso-host must not depend on Axum, Tauri, Flutter, or another presentation shell"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: no-query-cache
    severity: blocking
    description: "Do not add a query-cache dependency; the entity graph owns freshness"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: generated-theme-is-read-only
    severity: blocking
    description: "Do not hand-edit web/src/theme.css or mobile/lib/core/theme/tokens.dart; edit tokens.toml and regenerate"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: no-console-log-in-web-source
    severity: blocking
    description: "No console.log statements in web TypeScript source"
    check: "rg -n 'console\\.log' web/src -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx'"

  - id: no-any-type-in-web-source
    severity: blocking
    description: "No explicit any type in web TypeScript source"
    check: "rg -n ': any([,;)>]|$)' web/src -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx'"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: "No hardcoded API keys, tokens, or passwords in application source"
    check: "rg -n 'sk-|api_key|API_KEY|secret.*=[[:space:]]*[\"'\"'][A-Za-z0-9]' crates web/src mobile/lib desktop/src-tauri/src"
```

## Warning Constraints

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    description: "Tests exist for every new behavior introduced by a change"

  - id: lint-clean
    severity: warning
    description: "Architecture, Rust, web, and Flutter lint checks pass without warnings"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets && pnpm --dir web lint && flutter analyze mobile"

  - id: no-stub-comments
    severity: warning
    description: "No TODO, FIXME, STUB, or HACK comments are introduced"
    check: "rg -n 'TODO|FIXME|STUB|HACK' crates web/src mobile/lib desktop/src-tauri/src"

  - id: accessibility-basics
    severity: warning
    description: "New UI uses semantic HTML/widgets, keyboard access, labels, and visible focus states"
    note: "Manual review is required"

  - id: exact-dependency-pins
    severity: warning
    description: "Preserve exact pins for code-generation and FFI dependency graphs unless the full coherent set is validated"
```

## Workflow Triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "cargo build --workspace && pnpm --dir web build && flutter analyze mobile"

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "cargo test --workspace && flutter test mobile"
```

## Project Notes

- The focus project is the repository root; no multi-root VS Code workspace was found.
- `web/openspec/config.yaml` is nested below the focus root and has no specs, so KBD uses its built-in change management until a root OpenSpec project or actual specs are added.
- Design intent comes from `docs/design/`; sequencing comes from `docs/plan/build-order.md`; architecture decisions come from `docs/architecture/`.

+//! Session authority shared by every shell. Credentials never serialize.
+
+use std::sync::Arc;
+
+use async_trait::async_trait;
+use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+use uuid::Uuid;
+
+use crate::{
+    domain::{ActorId, PracticeId},
+    ports::Clock,
+};
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum Principal {
+    User,
+    Agent,
+    Service,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+pub struct VerifiedSession {
+    pub actor: ActorId,
+    pub practice: PracticeId,
+    pub principal: Principal,
+    pub on_behalf_of: Option<ActorId>,
+}
+
+impl VerifiedSession {
+    pub fn may_attempt_clinical_act(&self) -> bool {
+        matches!(self.principal, Principal::User)
+    }
+}
+
+/// Opaque input accepted only by the trusted identity adapter. No Debug or
+/// Serialize implementation: logging a request must not disclose a credential.
+pub enum SessionCredential {
+    Cookie(String),
+    NativeToken(String),
+}
+
+/// Produced by server-side whoami validation, never from caller identity hints.
+pub struct AuthenticatedIdentity {
+    pub identity_id: Uuid,
+    pub session_id: Uuid,
+    /// Set by the trusted identity adapter, never by a request header or trait.
+    pub principal: Principal,
+    pub expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
+}
+
+pub struct Membership {
+    pub user_id: Uuid,
+    pub practice_id: Uuid,
+    pub display_name: String,
+    pub capabilities: Vec<String>,
+    pub authorization_revision: String,
+}
+
+/// A noncredential projection. It grants no authority to subsequent commands.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
+pub struct SessionSummary {
+    pub identity_id: Uuid,
+    pub session_id: Uuid,
+    pub user_id: Uuid,
+    pub practice_id: Uuid,
+    pub display_name: String,
+    pub principal: Principal,
+    pub capabilities: Vec<String>,
+    pub expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
+    pub authorization_revision: String,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
+pub enum SessionError {
+    #[error("authentication required")]
+    Unauthenticated,
+    #[error("additional authentication required")]
+    ReauthenticationRequired,
+    #[error("practice access denied")]
+    PracticeDenied,
+    #[error("session service unavailable")]
+    Unavailable,
+    #[error("native authentication unavailable")]
+    NativeAuthenticationUnavailable,
+}
+
+#[async_trait]
+pub trait IdentityProvider: Send + Sync {
+    async fn authenticate(
+        &self,
+        credential: &SessionCredential,
+    ) -> Result<AuthenticatedIdentity, SessionError>;
+}
+
+#[async_trait]
+pub trait MembershipRepository: Send + Sync {
+    async fn resolve(
+        &self,
+        identity: &AuthenticatedIdentity,
+        practice: Option<Uuid>,
+    ) -> Result<Membership, SessionError>;
+}
+
+#[async_trait]
+pub trait SessionPort: Send + Sync {
+    async fn resolve(
+        &self,
+        credential: &SessionCredential,
+        practice: Option<Uuid>,
+    ) -> Result<SessionSummary, SessionError>;
+}
+
+pub struct SessionService {
+    pub identities: Arc<dyn IdentityProvider>,
+    pub memberships: Arc<dyn MembershipRepository>,
+    pub clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
+}
+
+#[async_trait]
+impl SessionPort for SessionService {
+    async fn resolve(
+        &self,
+        credential: &SessionCredential,
+        practice: Option<Uuid>,
+    ) -> Result<SessionSummary, SessionError> {
+        let identity = self.identities.authenticate(credential).await?;
+        if identity.expires_at <= self.clock.now() {
+            return Err(SessionError::Unauthenticated);
+        }
+        if identity.principal != Principal::User {
+            return Err(SessionError::PracticeDenied);
+        }
+        let membership = self.memberships.resolve(&identity, practice).await?;
+        // A slow database read cannot extend the validated credential's life.
+        if identity.expires_at <= self.clock.now() {
+            return Err(SessionError::Unauthenticated);
+        }
+        Ok(SessionSummary {
+            identity_id: identity.identity_id,
+            session_id: identity.session_id,
+            user_id: membership.user_id,
+            practice_id: membership.practice_id,
+            display_name: membership.display_name,
+            principal: identity.principal,
+            capabilities: membership.capabilities,
+            expires_at: identity.expires_at,
+            authorization_revision: membership.authorization_revision,
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// Clean-checkout composition refuses authenticated session work until configured.
+pub struct UnavailableSessions;
+
+#[async_trait]
+impl SessionPort for UnavailableSessions {
+    async fn resolve(
+        &self,
+        _: &SessionCredential,
+        _: Option<Uuid>,
+    ) -> Result<SessionSummary, SessionError> {
+        Err(SessionError::Unavailable)
+    }
+}

+    def roles_present(self):

+    def with_role_tracking(self, action):
+        # Snapshot immediately around each role-creating bootstrap/migration,
+        # including partial failures; preserve every role present beforehand.
+        before = self.roles_present()
+        try:
+            return action()
+        finally:
+            added = self.roles_present() - before
+            self.created_roles.update(added)
+            for role in added:
+                self.sql("postgres", "COMMENT ON ROLE " + identifier(role) + " IS " + literal(self.name) + ";")

+    def run_process(self, label, command, env):
+        self.mark(label)
+        entry = {"label": label, "command": command, "return_code": None}
+        self.report["processes"].append(entry)
+        process = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, cwd=ROOT, text=True,
+                                   stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                   start_new_session=True)
+        try:
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=self.args.command_seconds)
+        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, KeyboardInterrupt) as error:
+            entry["timed_out"] = isinstance(error, subprocess.TimeoutExpired)
+            # Cargo can leave a test or migration child alive if only its own
+            # process is killed. Stop this runner's process group before DB cleanup.
+            try:
+                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
+                process.communicate(timeout=10)
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+                process.communicate(timeout=10)
+            except ProcessLookupError:
+                process.communicate(timeout=10)
+            entry["return_code"] = process.returncode
+            raise
+        completed = subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)
+        entry["return_code"] = completed.returncode
+        # Do not serialize panic messages or logs: they may carry connection
+        # parameters. Only strict synthetic assertions and Rust totals leave.
+        output = completed.stdout + "\n" + completed.stderr
+        entry["actual_result_output"] = [
+            line.strip() for line in output.splitlines()
+            if re.fullmatch(r"gate_transaction_check: [a-z][a-z0-9_]*", line.strip())
+            or re.fullmatch(r"test [a-zA-Z0-9_:]*gate_transaction_lifecycle \.\.\. (ok|FAILED)", line.strip())

The desktop function is a wrapper contract without active Tauri command registration. The web shell still returns a fail-closed placeholder for graph-backed gate navigation; RA14 owns the consuming selector.

The RA04 outcome for `gate_affirmed_at` is bounded to the authoritative producer, approved projection, mounted route preservation and navigation handoff. RA05 owns the committed transition through the live Electric stream.

Broad phase T2, release T3, production deployment, browser rendering, Tauri IPC, Tauri windows and physical-device behavior were not run. # flint-gate configuration for local docker compose.
#
# Copied from flint-gate/config.example.yaml (2026-09-06) with exactly two
# changes for containerized use:
#   database.url  localhost -> db        Postgres is a compose service
#
# admin_listen stays on LOOPBACK. Widening it to 0.0.0.0 makes flint-gate
# refuse to start unless server.admin_auth is set — a deliberate fail-safe
# against exposing an unauthenticated control plane, and it fired when this
# config was first written. admin_auth needs a real JWKS-backed provider, so
# the correct local answer is to keep the admin API loopback-only and reach it
# with `docker compose exec`, not to invent a fake issuer.
#
# The example already targets http://kratos:4433, so the auth provider needed
# no change. admin_auth is left unset: the admin port is published only to the
# developer's own host here. Binding it non-loopback in any shared environment
# REQUIRES setting admin_auth — see the comment in the server block below.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Flint Gate — Example Configuration
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy this file to config.yaml and edit for your environment.
# Hot-reload: changes to config.yaml are applied within ~200ms.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

server:
  # Proxy server — receives all inbound traffic. Expose to the internet.
  listen: "0.0.0.0:4456"
  # Admin API bind. Defaults to loopback. When you widen this bind to a
  # non-loopback address you MUST also set `admin_auth` below — flint-gate
  # refuses to start on a non-loopback admin bind without authentication
  # (fail-safe against exposing an unauthenticated control plane).
  admin_listen: "127.0.0.1:4457"
  # Admin API authentication. Omit for an UNAUTHENTICATED loopback-only admin
  # API (local development). Set it to require auth on every admin request
  # (all routes except the /health and /ready probes). Reuses an ordinary auth
  # provider — `type: jwt` (Bearer, e.g. an Ory Hydra-issued token) or
  # `type: kratos` (session cookie). Any JWKS-backed JWT provider works.
  # admin_auth:
  #   provider:
  #     type: jwt
  #     jwks_url: "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
  #     issuer: "https://auth.example.com"
  #     audience: "flint-admin"
  # Allow plaintext http:// upstream URLs (Hydra token/admin endpoints). OFF by
  # default: flint-gate refuses to start with an http:// hydra_token_url or
  # hydra_admin_url, because those calls forward a subject_token / client
  # credentials and must not travel in cleartext. Set true ONLY for local dev
  # against an http:// Hydra (a loud WARN is logged when enabled).
  allow_insecure_upstream: false
  # Agent-governance lint. flint-gate WARNs when an AGENT-REACHABLE route (its auth
  # provider is `jwt` or `mcp` — JWKS-backed, can carry an agent token) is
  # under-governed: a token budget left at a non-agent scope (agent spend not
  # counted under the Agent scope), no `authorize` hook (ungoverned tool calls), or
  # a scope:agent + window:lifetime budget (can't fail closed). The lint covers the
  # MERGED (YAML + database) route set actually served — including DB routes added
  # via database.override_yaml and hot-reload, not just YAML. When true (the
  # default), any agent-reachable route (JWT/MCP auth) without an `authorize`
  # hook causes a hard startup error, or a hot-reload rejection that retains the
  # last-good router. Set false ONLY for legacy routes that cannot yet add an
  # authorization hook — understand you are running without Cedar evaluation for
  # those routes.
  # Default: true (fail-closed).
  strict_agent_governance: true
  # To disable for a legacy deployment that has not yet added authorize hooks:
  # strict_agent_governance: false
  # Refuse to start when the initial Cedar policy set is empty (no policies
  # loaded from the DB). Off by default: an empty set is a valid fail-closed
  # (default-deny) posture. Enable only when you REQUIRE explicit Cedar
  # policies before the proxy accepts any traffic.
  # Has no effect when `database:` is not configured.
  require_policies_at_startup: false
  # Per-credential rate limiting for the admin router's PROTECTED endpoints
  # (everything except /health, /ready, and /metrics). Uses tower-governor with
  # the same CredentialKeyExtractor as the proxy surface — rate-limits are keyed
  # by the caller's credential (Bearer token, session cookie), not by IP, so a
  # shared ingress/NAT does not let one admin credential starve others.
  #
  # Recommended for any admin bind reachable beyond localhost. For a loopback-only
  # admin bind this is defense-in-depth against local scripted abuse.
  #
  # Note: this limiter is per-replica in-process (no shared Redis backend).
  # In a multi-replica deployment each replica limits independently. Use a
  # network ingress rate-limiter (e.g. Nginx, Envoy, or cloud WAF) for a
  # cross-replica accurate ceiling on the admin surface.
  #
  # admin_rate_limit:
  #   enabled: true
  #   per_second: 5     # sustained token refill rate (requests / second)
  #   burst: 10         # burst capacity on top of the sustained rate
  tls:
    enabled: false
    # cert_path: "/etc/flint-gate/tls/cert.pem"
    # key_path: "/etc/flint-gate/tls/key.pem"
    # fail_open: false   # PRODUCTION: keep false (default). A cert load failure aborts startup.
    #                    # Set to true ONLY in development to fall back to plain TCP on cert errors.

database:
  url: "postgres://flint:flint@db:5432/flintgate"
  max_connections: 20
  # When true, routes stored in gate_routes take precedence over YAML routes.
  override_yaml: false

cache:
  l1:
    max_capacity: 10000
    ttl_seconds: 60
  l2:
    enabled: false
    # redis_url: "redis://localhost:6379"
    # IMPORTANT (multi-replica): when server.rate_limit.enabled is true and
    # you run more than one replica (e.g. a Kubernetes Deployment with replicas > 1),
    # each pod maintains its own in-memory counter. Agents can bypass limits by
    # spreading requests across replicas. Set redis_url here to share counters
    # across all replicas and enforce a true per-identity budget.
  # Postgres LISTEN channel for real-time cache invalidation
  invalidation_channel: "flintgate_config_changed"

# ─── Auth Providers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each entry is a named provider. Routes reference providers by name.

auth_providers:
  kratos_session:
    type: kratos
    base_url: "http://kratos:4433"
    forward_cookies: true
    session_cookie: "ory_kratos_session"

  bearer_jwt:
    type: jwt
    jwks_url: "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
    issuer: "https://auth.example.com"
    audience: "flint-gate"
    leeway_seconds: 5

  api_key:
    type: api_key
    header: "X-API-Key"
    store: database

  passthrough:
    type: anonymous
    default_subject: "anonymous"

# ─── Outbound JWT Minting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Used by the claims_enhancement hook to mint JWTs for upstream services.

jwt:
  signing_algorithm: "HS256"
  # For production use RS256/ES256 with key files instead:
  # signing_key_path: "/etc/flint-gate/keys/private.pem"
  signing_key_secret: "change-me-in-production-use-a-strong-secret"
  issuer: "https://gate.example.com"
  default_ttl_seconds: 300

# ─── Token Exchange (RFC 8693) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Gateway-local OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange at `POST /oauth/token`. An agent
# exchanges a user's `subject_token` for a DOWNSCOPED delegated token carrying an
# `act` claim — the user's raw token is never forwarded upstream. The
# subject_token is verified against `subject_token_provider`'s JWKS, so ANY IdM
# that issues a verifiable JWT (Ory Hydra is the reference) is a valid source.
# Disabled by default.
token_exchange:
  enabled: false
  # An auth_providers entry (must be JWKS-backed: type jwt or mcp).
  subject_token_provider: bearer_jwt
  # delegated_ttl_seconds: 300   # falls back to jwt.default_ttl_seconds
  # Federate-first: proxy the exchange to an Ory Hydra token endpoint (Hydra owns
  # RFC 8693) instead of minting locally. Requires hydra_token_url. On a Hydra
  # transport/non-2xx error the exchange fails closed (deny) — no local fallback.
  # CAVEAT: Hydra has known `aud`-handling quirks when exchanging EXTERNAL tokens
  # (ory/hydra#3723) — validate your Hydra audience config before relying on it.
  # delegate_to_hydra: false
  # hydra_token_url: "https://hydra.example.com/oauth2/token"
  # NOTE: an `actor_token` (multi-hop delegation) is rejected (400 invalid_request)
  # — single-hop `act` only this release.
  # NOTE: in delegate mode the RELAYED Hydra token carries Hydra's claims, NOT the
  # gateway's signed flint_kind=agent marker — so delegate-issued tokens are NOT
  # gateway-classified as Agent and escape the gateway-side agent budget/rate limit
  # (by design: federate, never an IdP). Watch the share of traffic taking this path
  # via `flint_delegate_total{result=...}` on the admin metrics endpoint (:4457/metrics).

# ─── OAuth 2.0 (client credentials + introspection) ───────────────────────────
# client_credentials: service-to-service (non-human) identity. Clients live in
#   the `oauth_clients` table (create via the admin API); a client authenticates
#   with client_id + client_secret at `POST /oauth/token` and receives a minted
#   gateway service token. Where Ory Hydra is the AS, prefer Hydra's own grant.
# introspection: RFC 7662 `POST /oauth/introspect` for gateway-MINTED tokens.
#   `introspection_delegate` forwards opaque, Hydra-issued tokens to Hydra
#   (which owns RFC 7662 for its own tokens). Off unless set.
oauth:
  client_credentials_enabled: false   # requires a database (client store)
  introspection_enabled: false
  # RFC 7662 §2.1 REQUIRES authenticating the introspection endpoint (token-scanning
  # defense). Defaults to true: /oauth/introspect requires OAuth client credentials
  # (client_id/client_secret via HTTP Basic or form), verified against oauth_clients.
  # Set false ONLY when the endpoint is network-restricted to trusted callers.
  introspect_auth: true
  # Per-endpoint rate limiting for /oauth/token + /oauth/introspect (independent of
  # server.rate_limit). Throttles the client-credentials guessing surface + the
  # introspection oracle. When a shared Redis limiter is configured (cache.l2) the
  # counters are authoritative ACROSS REPLICAS; otherwise an in-process governor
  # applies (per-replica).
  rate_limit:
    enabled: false
    per_second: 5
    burst: 10
    # Strict cross-replica mode (off by default). When true, flint-gate REFUSES to
    # start if the OAuth surface is exposed on a non-loopback bind but no SHARED
    # limiter is configured (cache.l2.enabled + cache.l2.redis_url). Without a
    # shared limiter each replica limits independently, so the effective ceiling
    # scales with the replica count — set this when you need a cross-replica-accurate
    # limit to be an enforced invariant rather than a silent per-replica degrade.
    require_shared_backend: false
  # What to do if the shared Redis limiter is unreachable mid-request:
  #   deny    — fail closed (default; REQUIRED posture for the introspection oracle)
  #   degrade — fall back to the in-process governor + WARN (token endpoint only;
  #             avoids an availability cliff on a Redis blip)
  # The introspection endpoint always denies; this setting governs the token
  # endpoint's fallback and lets an operator force uniform `deny`.
  on_backend_unavailable: deny
  # service_token_ttl_seconds: 300
  # introspection_delegate:  # only reachable AFTER introspect client-auth
  #   hydra_admin_url: "https://hydra-admin.example.com"

# ─── Agent tool-scope sugar ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ergonomic per-agent tool scoping that COMPILES to Cedar permit/forbid policies
# on Action::"call_tool" for the Agent::"<agent>" principal — a validated
# front-end over the policy engine, not a second authority. Each `allow` tool
# becomes a permit; each `deny` becomes a forbid (deny WINS — Cedar forbid
# overrides permit). A value with `*` is a glob matched against the tool name;
# otherwise it is an exact tool match. Compiled policies are validated at startup:
# an entry that produces invalid Cedar, or names an agent/tool with illegal
# characters, REFUSES to start (fail-closed). Empty by default.
#
# The compiled sugar is carried as an immutable overlay on the authorization engine
# and enforced ALONGSIDE any database policies (the live bundle is DB rows ++ sugar,
# and the overlay is re-applied on every reload — a policies reload never drops it).
# Cross-source conflicts resolve by Cedar forbid-overrides-permit. The overlay is
# fixed at startup from this file; changing it at runtime needs a restart (a
# config-sugar hot-reload is a follow-up).
agent_tool_policies: []
  # - agent: "ci-bot"
  #   allow: ["deploy", "run_tests"]
  #   deny:  ["delete_*"]

# ─── Human-in-the-loop approval ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# When a Cedar policy marks a tool call for approval (@require_approval on a
# permit), the streaming call PAUSES until a human approves/denies it via the
# admin API/UI. Fail-closed at every edge: an undecided approval AUTO-DENIES at
# `ttl_seconds` (the call is dropped, the stream resumes to termination — never
# hangs); `enabled: false` denies a RequireApproval outright (never pauses); a
# background janitor reaps expired entries.
#
# MULTI-REPLICA CONSTRAINT: The pending-approval table is in-memory PER REPLICA.
# A POST /approvals/:id/decision that reaches the wrong replica returns 404.
# Beta mitigation: apply k8s/service-admin.yaml (sessionAffinity: ClientIP) to
# pin each admin client to one replica. Known limitation: sticky session is lost
# on pod restart — any pending stream on the restarted pod is abandoned.
# Long-term fix (post-beta): Postgres-backed shared approval store.
approval:
  enabled: true
  # ttl_seconds: 300   # override the built-in default (300s)
  # max_pending: 1000  # cap on concurrent pending approvals; new RequireApproval
  #                    # decisions fail-closed to Deny when the table is full.
  #                    # Defaults to 1 000. Set to a smaller value in memory-constrained
  #                    # environments; raise it if you expect many concurrent approvals.
  # janitor_interval_seconds: 60   # how often the background janitor sweeps expired
  #                                # entries from the approval table. When unset,
  #                                # derived from ttl_seconds / 2 (clamped to [10, 300]),
  #                                # with a fallback of 60 s. Tune this independently
  #                                # when your TTL is very long and you want faster
  #                                # reclaim without shortening the approval window.

# ─── Sites ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A site maps one or more domains to a default auth provider and upstream.

sites:
  # Session discovery owns fresh Kratos + ASO membership validation in the
  # application. No Gate identity/cache result grants authority on this route.
  - id: "aso-session"
    domains: ["localhost:4456", "127.0.0.1:4456"]
    default_auth: passthrough
    default_upstream: "http://host.docker.internal:8787"

  - id: "my-app"
    domains:
      - "app.example.com"
      - "localhost:3000"
    default_auth: kratos_session
    default_upstream: "http://app-backend:3001"

  - id: "api"
    domains:
      - "api.example.com"
    default_auth: api_key
    default_upstream: "http://api-backend:8080"

# ─── Routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Routes are matched in priority order (higher priority first),
# then by path specificity (longer patterns first).

routes:
  # Fresh clinical policy is mandatory before forwarding. The callback resolves
  # raw Kratos credentials and ASO case scope; cached Gate identity grants nothing.
  # Requires the Gate build containing the aso_clinical_authorize hook.
  - id: "aso-gate-read"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/gate"
      methods: ["GET"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-gate-affirm"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/gate/affirm"
      methods: ["POST"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-gate-remove"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/gate/remove"
      methods: ["POST"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-gate-command"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/gate/commands/*"
      methods: ["GET"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-letter-sign"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/letters/*/sign"
      methods: ["POST"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-letter-sign-command"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/letters/*/sign/commands/*"
      methods: ["GET"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 101
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-evidence-reassess"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/evidence/*/state"
      methods: ["POST"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 101
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  - id: "aso-evidence-reassessment-command"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/cases/*/evidence/*/commands/*"
      methods: ["GET"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 101
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: aso_clinical_authorize
          config:
            url: "http://host.docker.internal:8787/internal/gate/authorize"

  # Keep upstream on the site: a route-level upstream replaces the query too.
  # This exact GET route preserves practiceId and all supported credentials;
  # the host returns no-store 200/401/403/503 after authoritative validation.
  - id: "aso-session"
    site: "aso-session"
    match:
      path: "/api/session"
      methods: ["GET"]
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100

  # /api/session/replica-grant is deliberately absent from the client-facing
  # route table. A configured claims_enhancement hook calls that ASO endpoint
  # as an internal upstream callback; clients receive only the resulting
  # authorized FRF facade response. RA05 owns that deployment composition.

  # ── LLM Chat (streaming) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: "chat-stream"
    site: "my-app"
    match:
      path: "/api/chat/**"
      methods: ["POST"]
    upstream: "http://llm-backend:8000/v1/chat/completions"
    auth: kratos_session
    priority: 10
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: claims_enhancement
          config:
            inject_headers:
              X-User-Id: "{{ identity.id }}"
              X-User-Email: "{{ identity.traits.email }}"
              X-Org-Id: "{{ identity.metadata_public.org_id }}"
            mint_jwt:
              enabled: true
              additional_claims:
                scope: "chat"
                org_id: "{{ identity.metadata_public.org_id }}"
        - type: body_transform
          config:
            set_fields:
              user: "{{ identity.id }}"
              model: "{{ coalesce(body.model, 'claude-sonnet-4-6') }}"
      post_response:
        - type: stream_meter
          config:
            log_to_db: true
    stream:
      enabled: true
      protocol: sse
      ai:
        ag_ui:
          enabled: true
          validate_events: true
          allowed_events:
            - TEXT_MESSAGE_START
            - TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT
            - TEXT_MESSAGE_END
            - TOOL_CALL_START
            - TOOL_CALL_ARGS
            - TOOL_CALL_END
            - RUN_STARTED
            - RUN_FINISHED
            - RUN_ERROR
            - STEP_STARTED
            - STEP_FINISHED
        a2ui:
          enabled: true
          allowed_intents:
            - render_component
            - show_toast
            - stream_content
          theme:
            mode: dark
            primary: "#2563eb"
        session_watchdog:
          enabled: true
          check_interval_seconds: 30
        backpressure:
          max_stream_duration_seconds: 300
          max_events: 10000

  # ── API Key Route (non-streaming) ─────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: "api-completions"
    site: "api"
    match:
      path: "/v1/completions"
      methods: ["POST"]
    upstream: "http://llm-backend:8000/v1/completions"
    auth: api_key
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: claims_enhancement
          config:
            inject_headers:
              X-Client-Id: "{{ api_key.client_id }}"
              X-Scopes: "{{ api_key.scopes }}"

  # ── Health check (no auth) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: "health"
    site: "my-app"
    match:
      path: "/health"
      methods: ["GET"]
    upstream: "http://app-backend:3001/health"
    auth: passthrough
    priority: 100

  # ── Catch-all (default upstream, Kratos auth) ─────────────────────────────
  - id: "catch-all"
    site: "my-app"
    match:
      path: "/**"
      methods: []
    auth: kratos_session
    priority: -1
    # No upstream set — uses site default_upstream (http://app-backend:3001)
    hooks:
      pre_request:
        - type: claims_enhancement
          config:
            inject_headers:
              X-User-Id: "{{ identity.id }}"

findings.claim: The replica_grant handler issues a ReplicaGrant without verifying the resolved session's principal is a human, unlike clinical_context which explicitly rejects non-User principals.
findings.evidence: clinical_context() contains `if session.principal != Principal::User { return Err(ClinicalContextError::NonHuman); }`, but replica_grant() only guards on `summary.expires_at > state.services.clock.now()` and then returns `Json(ReplicaGrant::for_session(&summary))`. The principal refusal exists only inside the SessionService implementation of SessionPort (crates/aso-host/src/session.rs), so any alternate/future SessionPort wiring that returns an Agent or Service summary produces a full five-projection grant. The axum tests inject GrantSessions/FixedGrantSessions directly, demonstrating the handler itself performs no principal check.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if summary.principal != Principal::User { return session_error(SessionError::PracticeDenied) }` (or a dedicated error) in replica_grant before constructing the grant, mirroring clinical_context.

Nothing in the packet shows a replacement HTTP or projection path for those endpoints.
findings.suggested_fix: Either confirm in the change evidence that routes::cases contained only legacy routes superseded by gate/evidence/projection paths, or restore the still-needed case endpoints under verified-context handlers.

findings.claim: The only FRF verifier hardcodes RS256 while the Gate deployment config mints HS256, so the Gate→FRF replica token path cannot interoperate as configured, and the packet's end-to-end evidence verifies the minted HS256 token with a Python hmac check instead of the actual FRF verifier.
findings.evidence: crates/frf-identity-ory/src/verifier.rs: `Validation::new(Algorithm::RS256)`. docker/flint-gate/config.yaml: `jwt: signing_algorithm: "HS256"`. scripts/test-replica-grant.py verifies the token locally (`hmac.new(SECRET.encode(), signed, hashlib.sha256)`) and never presents it to OryIdentityVerifier. Acceptance criterion 1.3 requires "expiry and issuer/audience validation across Gate and FRF" and 2.2 requires wrong issuer/audience rejected; no evidence in the packet runs a Gate-minted token through the real FRF verification path.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure an asymmetric signing key for the replica minter (or make the verifier algorithm part of validated config) and add a fixture that passes an actual Gate-minted token through OryIdentityVerifier with the deployed issuer/audience.

findings.claim: Issuer validation is conditional on optional config (`if let Some(issuer) = &self.issuer`), so a deployment that omits the issuer accepts any `iss` from a key-resolvable IdP, contrary to criterion 1.3/2.2's blanket claim that a wrong issuer is rejected.
findings.evidence: verifier.rs: `validation.set_audience(&[&self.audience]);` is unconditional, but `if let Some(issuer) = &self.issuer { ... }` gates the issuer check. Nothing in the packet shows the issuer being required at construction. Acceptance criterion 1.3: "expiry and issuer/audience validation across Gate and FRF"; 2.2: "wrong issuer/audience/scope/revision is rejected."
findings.suggested_fix: Make the expected issuer a required field of OryIdentityVerifier (fail construction without it) so `iss` is always validated.

findings.claim: Acceptance criterion 2.4 is marked complete, but its evidence is a stub facade echoing a canned JSON body containing `gate_affirmed_at: null` — no gate affirmation is removed in another session and nothing propagates through an authorized stream.
findings.evidence: Criterion 2.4: "when A committed gate affirmation is removed in another session, then The projected cases.gate_affirmed_at clears through the authorized stream." The test `authorized_shape_route_preserves_a_cleared_gate_summary` constructs `CountingFacade` whose `fetch` returns a fixed `body` and asserts the route echoes it; CountingAuthz always returns true. The completion evidence itself concedes "the live Gate-to-FRF-to-Electric exchange and deployment topology belong to RA05," which contradicts checking 2.4 as satisfied.
findings.suggested_fix: Reopen criterion 2.4 (mark it partially satisfied) until a fixture removes a committed affirmation in one session and observes the cleared field arrive through the real replica stream, or scope the criterion explicitly to the route-level pass-through that was actually proved.

findings.claim: The deployment config mounts eight clinical routes on the `aso_clinical_authorize` hook and the new replica-grant minter reuses that module's `credential_headers`/`callback_url`, but the hook module's source is not in the packet, so the fail-closed behavior of the clinical boundary and the replica credential forwarding cannot be verified.
findings.evidence: config.yaml adds `type: aso_clinical_authorize` hooks for gate/sign/reassess routes with the comment "Requires the Gate build containing the aso_clinical_authorize hook." crates/flint-gate-core/src/middleware/mod.rs adds `mod aso_clinical_authorize;`, and aso_replica_grant.rs calls `super::aso_clinical_authorize::credential_headers(original_headers)?` and `super::aso_clinical_authorize::callback_url(&config.url)?` — yet supplemental_diffs includes only aso_replica_grant.rs, not aso_clinical_authorize.rs. Whether it enforces single-credential extraction, scheme/host pinning of the callback URL, and fail-closed mapping is unreviewable.
findings.suggested_fix: Include crates/flint-gate-core/src/middleware/aso_clinical_authorize.rs in the review packet (or its prior-waypoint review artifact) so the credential-forwarding and URL-validation helpers the replica path depends on are covered.

findings.claim: The duplicate `ory_kratos_session` cookie detection is bypassable with whitespace before the `=` (e.g., `ory_kratos_session =a`), because only the whole pair is trimmed before `split_once('=')`, leaving a trailing space in the key.
findings.evidence: credential(): `pair.trim().split_once('=').is_some_and(|(key, _)| key == "ory_kratos_session")` — for the pair ` ory_kratos_session =a`, trim yields `ory_kratos_session =a` and the key is `ory_kratos_session ` (trailing space), which fails the equality check, so a header containing `ory_kratos_session=a; ory_kratos_session =b` passes the duplicate rejection the comment says is required.
findings.suggested_fix: Trim the key before comparing: `pair.split_once('=').is_some_and(|(key, _)| key.trim() == "ory_kratos_session")`.

findings.claim: The mutually-exclusive configuration of `aso_replica_grant` and `mint_jwt` on one route is detected per-request at runtime (returning 503) instead of at config load/startup.
findings.evidence: pipeline.rs: `if let Some(replica_cfg) = &config.aso_replica_grant { if config.mint_jwt.is_some() { return Err(StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE); } ... }`. A misconfigured route starts cleanly and only fails when first exercised; with hot-reload this also means a bad route can be live-rejected only at request time.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the `aso_replica_grant` + `mint_jwt` conflict in config validation (alongside the other route linting in config/types.rs) so startup or hot-reload refuses the route.

findings.claim: The duplicate-`ory_kratos_session` cookie rejection is bypassable with whitespace before the `=` sign, defeating the stated anti-ambiguity control.
findings.evidence: credential(): `pair.trim().split_once('=').is_some_and(|(key, _)| key == "ory_kratos_session")` — for the pair ` ory_kratos_session =b`, trim removes only outer whitespace, so the key retains a trailing space (`ory_kratos_session `) and fails the equality check. A header `ory_kratos_session=a; ory_kratos_session =b` carries two session cookies yet passes the duplicate guard, even though the function's comment says it exists to "Reject ambiguous credential sources so the gateway and service cannot authenticate different identities from the same request." Prior review flagged this and it was left unchanged; the resolution ("no duplicate-cookie bypass was used to derive a grant in evidence") does not fix the parsing gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Trim the key before comparing: `pair.split_once('=').is_some_and(|(key, _)| key.trim() == "ory_kratos_session")`.

findings.claim: Changing `jti` from tolerated-optional to a required UUID claim tightens verification for every FRF lane (publish, subscribe, agents, signal), not just the ASO replica path, with no packet evidence that other lanes' token issuers always supply a UUID `jti`.
findings.evidence: Diff changes `pub jti: Option<String>` (previously `Uuid::parse_str(jti).unwrap_or_else(|_| Uuid::new_v4())` on parse failure, and `SessionId::new()` when absent) to `pub jti: String` with `Uuid::parse_str(&claims.jti).map_err(...)`. Any existing FRF client whose token omits `jti` or carries a non-UUID `jti` is now rejected gateway-wide. The new tests cover only the replica claim shape; no fixture demonstrates a non-ASO (event-lane) token still verifying.
findings.suggested_fix: Either confirm with a fixture that all existing FRF token issuers emit UUID `jti` claims, or scope the strict `jti` requirement to the ASO replica contract (e.g., enforce UUID jti only inside `aso_replica_scope`) while preserving prior behavior for other lanes.

findings.claim: ASO's credential extractor accepts whitespace-only header values that Gate's equivalent helper rejects, leaving the two boundaries with inconsistent input hygiene.
findings.evidence: ASO credential() checks only `value.is_empty()`; flint-gate's aso_clinical_authorize::credential_headers rejects `value.as_bytes().iter().all(u8::is_ascii_whitespace)`. A request reaching ASO directly (the server is also host-published on 8787 per docker/flint-gate/config.yaml upstreams) with `X-Session-Token: " "` produces SessionCredential::NativeToken(" ") and an unnecessary identity-provider round trip instead of an immediate 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror Gate's check: reject values that are empty or entirely ASCII whitespace in credential().

findings.claim: The deployment config documents the aso_clinical_authorize hook contract but records no constraint that any future aso_replica_grant route must authenticate with the Kratos session provider, a coupling only discoverable at request time.
findings.evidence: pipeline.rs requires `matches!(auth_method, AuthMethod::KratosSession)` inside aso_replica_grant::mint, returning 403 otherwise, and rejects a mint_jwt/asо_replica_grant conflict with a per-request 503. A future operator enabling the hook with `auth: passthrough` (the aso-session site default used throughout this config) would get a running route that fails every request, with no startup or lint signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a config-validation rule (alongside agent_governance_lint) that refuses aso_replica_grant on a route whose auth provider is not the Kratos session provider, and that rejects the mint_jwt conflict at load/hot-reload rather than per request.

findings.claim: The current_session handler lacks the independent expiry and principal guards that were added to replica_grant after prior review, so an injected SessionPort returning an expired or non-human summary yields a 200 with a valid-looking session from /api/session.
findings.evidence: replica_grant() now contains `Ok(summary) if summary.expires_at <= state.services.clock.now() => session_error(Unauthenticated)` and `Ok(summary) if summary.principal != Principal::User => session_error(PracticeDenied)`, and clinical_context() performs the same two checks. current_session() ends at `Ok(summary) => Json(summary).into_response()` with no handler-level check. The completion report claims the session boundary "independently refuses expired and non-human sessions"; the prior-review resolution ("fixed with observed red/green HTTP 200 to 403 proof") applied that handler-level defense only to the grant route. The production SessionService does enforce both conditions, so the gap is reachable only with a substituted port — but the handler tests in this same file demonstrate exactly that injection seam, and the fix pattern was already judged necessary one function below.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same two guards in current_session before serializing the summary (expiry against state.services.clock.now(), principal == Principal::User), mirroring replica_grant.

findings.claim: The Gate deployment config routes /api/session but not /api/session/replica-grant, so the grant endpoint is unreachable through the gateway for any external caller and is usable only via the host-published ASO port (8787) or Gate's internal hook callback.
findings.evidence: The routes block adds an exact GET route for `/api/session` ("This exact GET route preserves practiceId and all supported credentials") and eight aso_clinical_authorize clinical routes, but no route matching `/api/session/replica-grant`. The only consumer wired today is Gate's own claims_enhancement callback (`url: ".../api/session/replica-grant"` in the synthetic fixture config). If internal-only exposure is intended, the config comment block should say so explicitly; otherwise a same-shaped exact GET route is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add an exact-match passthrough route for /api/session/replica-grant mirroring the /api/session entry, or extend the comment to state the endpoint is deliberately internal-only.

findings.claim: Replica-mint failures propagate as a bare StatusCode via `.await?`, bypassing the no-store/Vary headers and typed JSON error body that the adjacent aso_clinical_authorize arm sets for its failures.
findings.evidence: The AsoClinicalAuthorize arm builds `(status, [(CACHE_CONTROL, "no-store"), (VARY, "Cookie, Authorization, X-Session-Token")], Json({"error": ...}))` before returning. The aso_replica_grant arm ends with `mint(...).await?`, where every error (401/403/503 from mint()) flows into the generic `Err(StatusCode)` path with no cache headers and no error code. Credential-bearing responses on this boundary are otherwise consistently marked non-cacheable.
findings.suggested_fix: Map the mint() error into the same response shape as the clinical-authorize arm (no-store, Vary, typed error JSON) instead of propagating a bare StatusCode.
